request.state: Without using decide, read reviews.jsonl and label each review as positive or negative.

hint.instructions: The user's message asks the agent for closed verdicts over text that it would otherwise read and judge piece by piece: a label, yes/no or score for each of many items (tickets, reviews, commits, failures, log lines, rows, commands, files), the one best match out of a long list of candidates (packages, files, helpers, options), one verdict per rule or acceptance criterion over a diff, a log or test output, or a verdict on each step or command before an action that is hard to undo.

criteria.true: The message asks for such verdicts, over a batch of items, a choice among many candidates, each rule or criterion held against evidence, or each step of something about to run.
criteria.false: The message asks the agent to do something (write, fix, edit, run, commit, rename, explain, summarise), asks for an exact fact (a count, a list of matches, a date, whether a command succeeded), or asks one question about one small thing.

batch-judgement.instructions: The message asks for a verdict, label or score on each of many items of text, or asks which of many items match a description.

criteria.true: It names a batch (a file of tickets, reviews, commits, failures, rows or commands, or "every", "each", "all of") and asks for a judgement on each item.
criteria.false: It asks about one item, asks for an exact list or count, or asks for no judgement at all.

pick-from-many.instructions: The message asks for the single best match out of many candidates (packages, libraries, files, helpers, options) listed somewhere.

criteria.true: There are many candidates and the user wants one of them picked.
criteria.false: There are only a few options, or no pick is asked for.

criteria-check.instructions: The message asks whether something meets a set of rules, criteria, requirements, a checklist, a policy or conventions.

criteria.true: A rule set is named or listed, and the user wants to know whether the work, diff or output meets it.
criteria.false: No rule set is involved, or the user asks to write or change the rules rather than check against them.

done-check.instructions: The message asks whether a task or change is done, complete, or ready to merge, ship or commit, judged from evidence such as a diff, test output or a task file.

criteria.true: The user asks for a verdict on whether the work is finished or ready.
criteria.false: The user asks for work to be done, or asks a factual question such as whether a command succeeded.

gate-check.instructions: Before an action that is hard to undo (commit, merge, push, deploy, release, running a script), the message asks whether it is safe, destructive or against the rules.

criteria.true: An action is about to happen and the user wants a safety or rules verdict first.
criteria.false: No such action is pending, or no verdict is asked for before it.
